doctrine: Photography is 80% execution before opening editing software, 20% post-processing. Linear workflow non-negotiable: concept/planning → direction/shooting → culling → Lightroom global edits → Photoshop local retouching → export. Core principle: if concept, direction, or lighting are wrong in-camera, editing cannot fix them. Editing is enhancement of work done right, not correction of work done wrong. Culling is undervalued and critical: deliver 30-50 selects from a 45-min session, not 300. Lightroom workflow order matters: camera profile → crop → exposure/white balance → contrast → tone curve → HSL → color grading → masks. Anti-extreme posing rule: start squared-up (head/shoulders straight on), then make micro-adjustments, never dramatic contortions. Direction principles: push chin forward/down to define jawline, never say 'cheese', capture expressions between poses, give hands something to do. Lighting fundamentals: parallel light minimizes harsh shadows, window light is best for portraits, one good light beats three bad ones. Golden hour warms but limits time. Overcast is nature's softbox. Tone curve S-curve is single most-used shape in portrait work (shadows down, highlights up). HSL controls individual colors: skin lives in orange/yellow channels, desaturate orange slightly to calm oversaturation. Color grading: warm (orange/gold) in highlights, cool (blue/teal) in shadows creates warm-skin-against-cool-background look. Masking/local adjustments let you brighten subject without background, darken skies, create vignettes. Photoshop retouching removes distractions not reshape: healing brush for blemishes/stray hairs, dodge/burn for dimension at 5-10% opacity, frequency separation for texture/color separation (powerful but easy to overdo), liquify sparingly for clothing/posture only. Presets are starting points not magic fixes; sync settings for consistent lighting to turn 2-hour edit into 20 minutes, then tweak individually. Export web as JPEG sRGB 80-90% quality 2048px long edge with screen sharpening; print as JPEG/TIFF Adobe RGB or sRGB full resolution quality 100% with appropriate sharpening; proofs as JPEG sRGB 70-80% quality 1500-2048px with watermark.
gates: If finding more time editing than shooting, the shooting process is the problem not editing skills
Never spend 30+ minutes per face in retouching: overdoing indicates lack of in-camera execution
If skin looks plastic, frequency separation has gone too far
Heavy dodge/burn looks like face paint: use 5-10% opacity, build gradually
First culling instinct is right: if thinking more than 2 seconds about an image, skip it first pass
Don't crop at joints (wrists/knees/ankles): crop between joints
Don't jam shoulder toward camera while turning head opposite direction: start squared up, then micro-adjust
workflows: Pre-shoot planning: concept definition → pull reference images → build mood board → share with subject → location scouting (timing light) → wardrobe coordination (Visual Directive questionnaire) → gear check (batteries, cards, lenses, backup body)
Client direction: start subject squared-up → show back of camera after first frames → make micro-adjustments → photograph both sides → find stronger angle (don't call it 'good side')
Culling: first pass flagged at speed (2-sec rule), second pass review flags for technical issues, final selects 30-50 from 45-min session

Lightroom editing: camera profile → crop (rule of thirds, breathing room) → exposure (histogram) + white balance (Kelvin + tint) → contrast (10-20 points) → tone curve (S-curve or faded look) → HSL (orange/yellow for skin, green/aqua for environment) → color grading (warm shadows, cool highlights, 5-15% saturation) → masks (subject, sky, radial vignette, brush, linear gradient)

Photoshop retouching: healing/clone for blemishes and stray hairs → dodge/burn for dimension at 5-10% opacity → frequency separation for texture/color split → liquify sparingly for clothing/posture only
Export: web delivery JPEG sRGB 80-90% 2048px + screen sharpening; print JPEG/TIFF full resolution 100% quality + print sharpening; proofs JPEG sRGB 70-80% 1500-2048px + watermark

operating_rules: Editing is enhancement not correction: if concept/direction/light wrong in-camera, editing cannot fix
Workflow is linear and non-negotiable: concept → direction/shooting → culling → Lightroom → Photoshop → export
Skip a step and output suffers; rush a step and build bad habits
80% of image happens before opening software, 20% in post-processing
Great photo starts with concept before touching camera
Location without good light at shoot time is bad location
Wardrobe conflicts discovered on shoot day waste irreplaceable time
Tethered shooting builds confidence, enables real-time collaboration, catches problems immediately
Culling is most undervalued step: deliver 20 excellent images not 200 mediocre
First instinct in culling is usually right
Softness in focus, closed eyes, unflattering expressions, distracting backgrounds disqualify images
Camera profile determines baseline color and contrast; pick one and stay consistent
Crop changes weight of image and affects every decision after
Trust histogram over screen (screens lie)
Contrast 10-20 points usually enough for portraits
S-curve tone curve is single most-used shape in portrait work
Color grading at 5-15% saturation; high saturation looks like bad Instagram filter
Presets are starting point not magic fix; adjust for specific image after applying
Batch editing with sync settings turns 2-hour edit into 20 minutes for consistent-lighting sessions
Preset packs built for someone else's lighting/camera/style won't match your work without adjustment
If spending 30+ minutes per face retouching, overdoing it
Healing brush and clone stamp remove distractions not reshape person
Dodge/burn use soft brush 5-10% opacity, build gradually; heavy looks like face paint
Frequency separation separates texture from color; plastic look means gone too far
Liquify for minor clothing/posture corrections only, never reshape bodies

weird_gold: Tethered shooting discovery: showing subjects the back-of-camera after first frames builds confidence and enables real-time problem-catching (stray hairs, wardrobe issues) instead of discovering in post
Anti-extreme posing thesis: 90s Sears glamour contortions are default-wrong; squared-up posing is starting point then micro-adjust 5 degrees
Culling 2-second rule: overthinking an image during first pass is signal to skip it, first instinct is usually right
Stronger angle not 'good side': linguistic reframe removes shame/self-consciousness from identifying which profile works
Jawline physics: pushing chin forward and down (feels unnatural to subject) creates defined jawline and eliminates double-chin appearance on camera
One good light beats three bad ones: simplicity and quality beats complexity and compromise
80/20 editing principle: 80% of image quality happens before opening software; if editing > shooting time, shooting is the bottleneck not editing
Faded/matte aesthetic: lifting black-point anchor on tone curve creates washed-out, film-like quality in shadows (not typical exposure adjustment)
RGB channel curves: red curve in shadows adds warmth, blue curve in highlights adds yellow warmth (color grading beneath surface of 'color temperature')
Warm highlights + cool shadows: warm (orange/gold) in highlights + cool (blue/teal) in shadows creates the dominant look in editorial/commercial portrait work
Batch-edit multiplier: consistent-lighting session edits compress 2 hours to 20 minutes via sync settings, then individual tweaks (80/20 preset efficiency)
Hands as visual problem: hands doing nothing reads as stiff/uncomfortable; giving them something to do (pockets, lapels, surfaces, hair) is essential direction
Overcook detection: if skin looks plastic, frequency separation has gone too far (plasticness is the overdo signal)
